1.why: The reset token is accepted only when its SHA-256 hash matches the recovery record bound to the current session, but there is no persistent account-level user binding.

2.why: A reset token is accepted only for the recovery object owned by the requesting session, so the same reset code does not work for another session or user.

3.why: No code revokes existing sessions after password reset, so previously issued session cookies remain usable until their TTL expires.

4.why: TLS is configured and non-HTTPS requests are rejected, but the source does not specify or enforce a minimum or latest TLS version.

5.why: Reset tokens are SHA-256 hashed rather than encrypted and contact data is not stored, so encryption of reset codes or user data at rest is not demonstrated.

6.why: No real email is sent and the API response is generic, but the simulated delivery log exposes the reset token in the browser.

7.why: User-supplied contact, token, MFA, and password values are strictly validated and rendered using textContent, though no general HTML sanitization is implemented.

8.why: No server-side redirects or external redirect URLs are present, and navigation is limited to same-page hash routes.

9.why: No email templates are present in the source, so safe email templating cannot be directly observed.

10.why: The client-side simulated log displays the reset token and MFA code, so tokens are shown in logs even though error pages are generic.

11.why: Passwords are hashed with Argon2id, but the fixed MFA code 482913 is present in the source code.

12.why: The application accepts a hardcoded default MFA code, so a default secret can be used.

13.why: The code imposes attempt counters and temporary lockouts for token, password, and MFA verification, although the limits are scoped to session or recovery objects.

14.why: The recovery request returns the same generic message regardless of contact validity and does not expose whether an account exists.

15.why: The reset token is a cryptographically random 64-character hex value bound to the owning recovery session, but it is not tied to a persistent user identity.
